title: An owner of fixed-cost assets turns idle capacity into waste, inverting optimization from minimizing use to maximizing productive work
body:
- Under metered pricing each unit costs money, so the rational response is to minimize use; idle time costs nothing.
- Owning the asset inverts this: baseline costs run whether or not the asset is used, so idle time turns paid money into zero output.
- The optimization flips from "use less" to "keep the asset productive" because productive work reclaims value that has already been paid for.
- A commercial provider paying the variable cost sees heavy always-on usage as eroding margins, while an owner bearing the fixed cost sees the same usage as recovering a wasting asset.
- This divergence means the same workload can be ruinous for one party and the rational move for the other.
conversion: idle capacity turns from a saving into a waste, inverting optimization from minimizing use to maximizing productive work
